summary.title: What helps people get comfortable on the command line?
summary.one_liner: Practical strategies, tools and resources, gathered from Mastodon replies, for overcoming fear of the command line: reducing risk, finding motivation, and learning tips.
keywords: how to get comfortable with the terminal
takeaways: Reduce risk on the command line with backups, git, tab completion instead of wildcards, safer rm aliases, and --dry-run options.
Use a 'killer app' like ripgrep, jq, or git, or lighter command line tools, to motivate regular terminal use.
Use fzf to fuzzy-pick files, git branches, or history, and pipe the choice into other commands.
Learn shortcuts and helpers such as Ctrl+R, cd -, less, explainshell, tldr and cheat sheets rather than memorizing everything.
A friendlier shell (fish, oh-my-zsh), a fancier prompt, aliases, and workshops or pairing with experienced users help build confidence.
summary.summary: Julia Evans asked people who had recently become comfortable with the command line what helped them, and compiled the replies into a list. The post is organized into three parts: reducing risks (backups, git, dry-run flags, safer rm, test machines), motivation (killer apps, inspiring examples, frustration with heavy GUI tools), and resources (explainshell, cheat sheets, fzf recipes, shell setups, workshops, books and videos). It is informal and anecdotal, with no single recommended path.
